page: OVHcloud r2-60 is a memory-optimized virtual server hosted on a KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Haswell processor running at 2.2 GHz. The system is configured with 4 physical cores and 1 thread per core, lacking hyper-threading. It provides a substantial memory capacity of 60.0 GB, translating to 15.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 100 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the underlying Intel Haswell architecture delivers modest processing speeds. The single-core stress-ng score of 763.28 and Geekbench single-core score of 880.0 place it in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance is also limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2676.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 4617.15, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is constrained, measuring 18.84 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 15.46 GB/sec for large-block write operations. However, the server achieves an average text generation speed of 83.62 tokens/second during small 135M LLM inference tests.

The r2-60 offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-performance compute cycles. By pairing a large 60.0 GB memory footprint with older, dedicated CPU hardware, it provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the premium cost of modern processor architectures. The primary tradeoff is the lower CPU performance and memory bandwidth, making it less suitable for compute-heavy tasks or real-time data processing. It is best suited for memory-bound applications such as caching layers, small database hosting, Redis instances, and lightweight background workers.
